content: Pre-Arrival Announcements for Passengers Script 1: All travelers, including those in transit, who have been in these countries within the past three weeks are required to report to the public health authority upon arrival at the airport. Thank you for your cooperation. Script 2: All travelers are required to complete a health declaration form before arrival. The information collected will be used in accordance with local privacy laws to help prevent the spread of the disease. Every traveler must complete a form, and parents or guardians may complete the form on behalf of children. The cabin crew will distribute the forms shortly. Please submit the completed form to the public health authority representative upon arrival. Thank you for your cooperation. Traveler Public Health Declaration Form If entry screening is implemented at points of entry in your country, public health authorities are advised to use a standardized form to harmonize international practices for primary health screening during the Ebola outbreak. The form collects information as part of the public health response to the Ebola outbreaks in West Africa. The data will be used in compliance with applicable national laws. Travelers are asked to provide details about symptoms experienced in the past 48 hours, such as fever, vomiting, diarrhea, severe headaches, unexplained bruising, or bleeding. Travelers must also list all countries visited in the past 21 days, including transit points, starting with the most recent. This includes questions about direct contact with bodily fluids of Ebola patients, providing care without protective equipment, or handling deceased bodies. The form also records clinical signs and symptoms, such as fever, vomiting, diarrhea, fatigue, muscle pain, or unexplained bleeding. Based on the assessment, public health authorities will determine the appropriate intervention, such as medical evaluation, transportation to a healthcare facility, or referral for symptom monitoring. Ill Traveler Card Travelers who may have been exposed to Ebola and are experiencing symptoms consistent with the disease will receive an informational card. This does not confirm an Ebola diagnosis but indicates the need for further medical evaluation. Ebola is a severe and often fatal disease transmitted through direct contact with the blood or bodily fluids of an infected person. Individuals are not contagious unless they exhibit symptoms such as fever, severe headache, muscle pain, vomiting, diarrhea, stomach pain, or unexplained bleeding or bruising. Public health officials will require medical evaluation, which may include testing for Ebola. Travelers will be transported to a hospital for examination and must follow all instructions to prevent exposing others. If Ebola is ruled out, travelers will be allowed to leave the hospital but must continue monitoring their health for 21 days. This includes taking their temperature twice daily, reporting symptoms, and avoiding public transportation or commercial travel. Travelers should notify public health officials if they plan to travel more than 50 miles or to another country. They should avoid public transportation and travel only by private car or ambulance, bringing the informational card to healthcare staff upon arrival.
